CHANGE 1336 IS UP: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1336 (commit 19ef26e0d4, NOT submitted, awaiting LLM-Review and Verified).

RE-VERIFIED ON THE FRESHEST origin/main after the operator asked whether this was a stale-repo artifact. IT IS NOT. At origin/main 9af88c3ada (which has advanced twice since this ticket was filed): rebar.toml's sections are still only [verify], [ticket], [mcp], [jira], [identity], bedrock mentions 0, and a clean-env resolution in a worktree at that commit still returns frontier -> anthropic:claude-opus-4-8, standard -> anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6, trivial -> anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5. The gap is real and current.

WHAT LANDS IN 1336. rebar.toml gains BOTH:
    [llm]
    model = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"
    [llm.model_classes]
    frontier = { model = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8" }
    standard = { model = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" }
    trivial  = { model = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0" }
Measured before/after in a clean env: the three classes flip from anthropic:* to the three bedrock: profiles, AND cfg.model flips from the bare literal 'claude-opus-4-8' to 'bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8'.

A CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S OWN APPROACH TEXT, which was mine and was imprecise. It says 'Do NOT set [llm] model as a scalar; use [llm.model_classes]'. What I MEANT was: do not use the scalar INSTEAD OF the class table. Both are required, and setting only the classes would have left a real leak open: cfg.model is a SECOND resolution path the class table cannot reach, defaulting to the bare literal 'claude-opus-4-8' which infers provider anthropic — the exact ambient-default leak [rebar:f124-f14a-fd62-4973] closed after MEASURING three tests calling direct Anthropic on non-Anthropic arms. Setting the scalar alone would instead collapse the frontier/standard split ([rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00]). So: scalar as COMPANION, never as substitute. The implementer flagged the contradiction rather than silently following the wrong half, which is the correct behaviour; the fault was in my wording, not their reading.

TESTS — 4 in tests/unit/test_project_default_provider.py, each mutation-verified RED with recorded output: the table removed (3 failed, including the cfg.model companion assertion); the rebar.toml id changed alone; the OVERLAY id changed alone (proving the pin is two-sided, not one); a class dropped (proving exact class-set equality); and the opt-out assertion inverted. Full offline suite 9808 passed / 42 skipped, exit 0, with ZERO existing tests modified.

WHY NO EXISTING TEST BROKE, which is worth recording because it looked like a serious risk. tests/conftest.py has an autouse fixture _default_rebar_root_to_sandbox that points REBAR_ROOT at a session-scoped EMPTY sandbox repo for every test. So no test resolves config against the real checkout's rebar.toml, and the tests that assert anthropic defaults were always testing the BUILT-IN FALLBACK AGAINST AN EMPTY CONFIG ROOT — not the project default. That is the distinction that decides whether such a test is stale or still correct, and here they are still correct as written. The implementer hit it as a genuine failure first (cfg.model resolving to the bare literal inside pytest while resolving to bedrock from the shell), which is the evidence for the classification rather than an assumption.

AC5 IS RESOLVED WITHOUT AN EPIC EDIT, and this closes the implementer's open question. AC5 asks that the epic-level claim the 'repo config / local env' switch is complete be corrected wherever it appears. I searched epic 061c's own description for 'repo config' / 'repo-config' / 'local env' / 'local dev': ZERO matching lines. The overstatement did not come from the epic or from any tracked file — it came from a git-ignored local handoff note (LOOP-PROMPT.local.md) written by a previous session. So there is nothing in the repo or the store to correct, and no epic description edit is warranted (which is also the safer outcome, since editing an epic's text can invalidate plan-review material pins on it and its children). AC5 is satisfied by this record.

STILL OWED BEFORE THE EPIC CAN CLOSE, per operator instruction: 1336 must MERGE, and LOCAL rebar use of Bedrock must then be CONFIRMED BY OBSERVATION — a real local LLM op whose per-call record shows bedrock: models. Configuring it is not the same as confirming it, and this ticket is not closed until the second half is evidenced.

# The project's authoritative config never got the Bedrock switch — only a per-developer opt-in was shipped

## Context / Problem

Epic 061c was tracked as having THREE permanent production switches: the repo config / local env, the
AWS review bot, and the CI external suite. The review bot is now cut over
[rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] and CI selects a provider through `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`. **The repo
config half was never done**, so every local gate run on this project still resolves to direct
Anthropic.

MEASURED, in a clean worktree at `gerrit/main` with no `REBAR_LLM_*` env set:

    merged [llm] file table keys: (EMPTY)
    model_classes present: False
      frontier -> anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
      standard -> anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6
      trivial  -> anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5

`rebar.toml` IS this project's authoritative config — `src/rebar/config.py` discovers
`rebar.toml` then `pyproject.toml`, and `read_reserved_section("llm", root)` reads a top-level
`[llm]` table from it. But `rebar.toml`'s only sections are `[verify]`, `[ticket]`, `[mcp]`,
`[jira]` and `[identity]`. There is no `[llm]` table, so the built-in class defaults apply and
those are unqualified names that infer provider `anthropic`.

**What WAS shipped, and why the tracking drifted.** [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] closed legitimately
against its own criteria: its Scope allowed "local LLM configuration only (the config file AND/OR
documented env for a developer machine)" and it chose the documented-env route —
`docs/local-dev-env.md:142-182` tells a developer to
`export REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE="/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam/.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml"`, explicitly labelled
"opt in", with a documented revert. So 1aa2 is not a false close; the epic-level summary that read
it as "repo config / local env — DONE" is what overstated it. Nobody has to opt in, and by default
nobody does.

**Why it matters rather than being cosmetic.** The epic's founding premise is that the path rebar
develops against is not the path rebar's users run, and that dogfooding closes the gap. A per-developer
opt-in that defaults OFF leaves that gap open for the local gates — which are the gates a developer
and every coding agent hit constantly. Observed while working eb6e: a local `rebar review-plan` ran
on `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` minutes after the production bot was verified on Bedrock.

## Scope

- `rebar.toml` — add an `[llm.model_classes]` table (the file is the project's authoritative config).
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — the opt-in section becomes an OPT-OUT section, since the default inverts.
- possibly a pinning test, so the ids cannot drift from `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml` (the same
  two-sided pin `tests/unit/test_reviewbot_bedrock_cutover.py` applies to the compose block).

## Approach — and the decision this ticket actually needs

The mechanical change is small; the DECISION is not, and should be made explicitly rather than by
committing a default:

* **Precedence makes it safe to try.** `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` OUTRANKS the project file, and env
  class slots outrank both, so CI arms that name a provider overlay (the external matrix, prompt-eval)
  are unaffected by a project default. The offline unit lanes make no LLM calls at all.
* **The cost is that every local gate then needs working AWS credentials.** A contributor without
  Bedrock access, or offline, would find their local gates failing where they used to work with an
  Anthropic key. That is a real onboarding regression and is the reason this is a decision, not a
  chore. Mitigation is a documented one-line opt-out (`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=…/anthropic.toml`),
  which is the mirror of what is documented today.
* Alternative considered: leave the default as Anthropic and instead make the opt-in loud (a
  `make` target, or a doctor warning). Cheaper, keeps onboarding intact, but does not close the
  dogfooding gap — it only advertises it.

Do NOT set `[llm] model` as a scalar; use `[llm.model_classes]`, or the per-pass frontier/standard
split collapses (the same trap [rebar:eb58-e71d-ec90-4b00] deprecated `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` for).

## Testing

- assert that in a clean checkout with no `REBAR_LLM_*` env and no `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`, the three
  classes resolve to `bedrock:` ids — i.e. the exact measurement above, inverted. Verify RED by
  removing the table.
- assert the ids are byte-equal to `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`, two-sided, so editing either
  file alone fails.
- assert the documented OPT-OUT works: with `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointed at the anthropic overlay,
  resolution returns to `anthropic:` — otherwise the escape hatch is unproven.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] the decision is recorded (project default Bedrock vs loud opt-in), with the onboarding cost
      stated, so it is a choice rather than a drift.
- [ ] if the default flips: `rebar.toml` carries an `[llm.model_classes]` table whose three ids are
      byte-equal to `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`, pinned two-sided by a test.
- [ ] a clean checkout with no LLM env resolves all three classes to `bedrock:` ids — recorded as
      observed output, since the current state was only discovered by measuring rather than reading.
- [ ] `docs/local-dev-env.md` documents the OPT-OUT (and no longer presents Bedrock as opt-in), and
      the opt-out is exercised once.
- [ ] the epic-level claim that the 'repo config / local env' switch is complete is corrected wherever
      it appears, so the next reader is not misled the way this was discovered.
compiled_state.title: Local dev still defaults to Anthropic: rebar.toml has no [llm] table, so the repo-config half of the Bedrock switch was never done
